title: The dogmatic vegan
text: If you hold the original line, that animals are not ours to use, you notice something strange. The pushback rarely comes from outsiders. It comes from inside the movement, from people who call themselves vegan but treat it as harm reduction. And you get the labels: purist, extremist, dogmatic, divisive. This is not new. In every justice movement in history, the people demanding real change were told they were too extreme, and the sharpest attacks came from the moderates on their own side. There are two incompatible ideas of veganism. One is a line: humans have no right to exploit animals, regardless of suffering. The other is a dial: anything that lowers the total suffering counts as a win. Purist only stings if being uncompromising about an injustice is a fault. No one wants an abolitionist who was flexible about slavery.
